pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks all seeded rows are 0 and that done=2 is rejected.
src/index.js default view is open; test 'AC-2' checks / and /?view=open list only the open items in id order.
Test 'AC-3' marks ids 3 and 1 done, then checks the done view returns '✓ First item' and '✓ Third item' in id order.
Test 'AC-4' checks the all view lists all three items in id order, with only the done one marked.
Test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav markup for each view and for /, with the current view as <strong> and not a link.
Object.hasOwn guard in src/index.js; test 'AC-6' checks Open, closed, empty and __proto__ each give 400 with no <li>.
Test 'AC-7' checks Nothing open., Nothing done yet. and No items yet. on all three views with an empty table; src/index.js falls back via a COUNT query.
traffic/routes.json lists /?view=done and /?view=all; test 'AC-8' checks routes.json contains both. The traffic worker passes the query through in `https://app.internal${path}`.

findings.what: The 'Follow-up edits' commit (a2f9c38) replaced `expect(app.seen.map(s=>s.path)).toEqual(["/healthz", ...ROUTES])` with `.toBeDefined()`. That assertion can never fail. The test no longer checks that the traffic worker requests /healthz and every listed route, which is the behaviour AC-8's synthetic traffic depends on. No spec decision justifies loosening it, and the PR claims 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', which is false.
findings.fix: Restore `expect(app.seen.map((s) => s.path)).toEqual(["/healthz", ...ROUTES])`. The fake app now records pathname+search, so it passes with the query routes.

findings.what: The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing'. A test was loosened in the last commit (toEqual changed to toBeDefined). The PR also omits the follow-up commit.
findings.fix: Restore the test and correct the PR body so it matches the diff.

findings.what: The README describes the views but does not say that traffic routes may now carry a query string, or that an invalid view gives 400.
findings.fix: Add one line about the 400 for a bad view and about query routes in traffic/routes.json.

lenses.note: The spec's decisions are followed: the list opens on open items, and the view is a GET query parameter.
All eight acceptance items are implemented and named by tests. The state table rows have tests, though the Done and All view tests don't check that no message shows.
The traffic route test was loosened to toBeDefined in a2f9c38. I did not run the tests; CI runs them on every push.
README updated for the views; a minor omission is noted.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ is rejected. The SQL fragments come from a constant table, not from user input.
No injection path: the view value is checked against fixed keys, and titles are HTML-escaped. The route regex now allows ? but still refuses spaces and #.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or style files; I judged it only through the tests.
No browser is available, and the PR has no screenshots.
The claim that no tests were loosened is false.
